title: Construction and Characterization of a Novel Vocal Fold Bioreactor
protocol: Make an aluminum mold with pre-determined inner and outer dimensions.
Fabricate a silicone membrane using the mold, featuring a central entrenched sleeve.
Create a pair of acrylic blocks with a circular opening in the middle.
Engrave matching ridges and grooves on the top and bottom acrylic blocks.
Sandwich the silicone membrane between the paired acrylic blocks.
Secure the assembly with four corner screws using a micro torque screwdriver set to 35 cN·m.
Mount a 3” extended range mini-woofer underneath the vibration chamber through corner screws on the bottom acrylic block.
Replicate seven additional vibration modules.
Affix four vibration modules to one stationary aluminum bar by placing the speaker bases in evenly spaced circular holes cut into the bar.
Stabilize each speaker by inserting a screw through the side of the aluminum bar into each circular hole.
Connect individual speakers to the selector by attaching wires to the positive and negative inputs on the speaker body then to the corresponding outputs on the selector.
Place two chamber arrays, the speaker selector and associated electronics in an anti-humidity enclosure.
House the entire assembly in a commercial cell culture incubator.
Feed main cables through medical grade PVC tubing connecting the power amplifier and speaker selector through the filter assembly at the back of the incubator.
Dissolve PCL pellets in chloroform at a concentration of 15 wt%.
Load the solution into a 10 ml syringe capped with a 21 G blunt-ended needle.
Lock the syringe onto a programmable syringe pump and set the flow rate at 1 ml/hr.
Place the aluminum foil-covered collector across from the needle horizontally, with a needle tip-to-collector distance of ~18 cm.
Clamp the positive alligator clip to the middle of the needle.
Attach the ground alligator clip to the aluminum collector.
Set the voltage on the high voltage power supply at 15 kV.
Turn on the syringe pump and power supply sequentially.
Clean the residual polymer solution around the needle tip with a dry paper towel.
Allow fibers to accumulate on the Al collector until thickness reaches ~250-300 µm (~7 hr under current conditions).
Store resultant scaffolds in a vacuum desiccator for 1-2 days to remove residual solvent.
Image scaffolds, sputter coated with gold, using Scanning Electron Microscope to show consistent fiber morphology.
Punch a cylindrical disk (diameter: 8 mm) out of the as-spun PCL mat using a 12 mm diameter biopsy punch.
Score four 2 mm long notches around the circular blade evenly spaced using an 8 mm biopsy punch.
Cut the edges of the arms outward with a scalpel blade.
Insert the scaffold into the groove of the silicone membrane via the extended arms.
Flatten the inserted scaffold by gently pressing its surface using flathead tweezers.
Attach a small piece of thin Al foil (8 mm x 2 mm, orthogonal shape) to the PCL scaffold to aid laser reflection.
Secure the assembled silicone membrane/PCL scaffold in the vibration chamber.
Add 1.5 ml water to the chamber to hydrate the PCL scaffold before vibration.
Introduce vibration signals (e.g., 200 Hz sinusoidal waves with a peak-to-peak voltage of 0.1 V) to the sandwiched acrylic chamber using the function generator.
Measure the voltage at each speaker input accurately with a voltmeter.
Assemble the single-point LDV and secure the fiber-optic laser sensor head to a pan-tilt head tripod.
Angle the sensor head so that it is pointing perpendicular to the tabletop.
Connect the LDV sensor head to the data acquisition module via coaxial cable, then connect the module to the laptop via USB.
Focus the laser beam perpendicularly at various predetermined points on the silicone membrane.
Click “Acquisition Settings” from the “Options” menu in the data acquisition software.
Change the measurement mode to “FFT”.
Click the “Continuous Measurement” option in the main toolbar.
Click the peak that forms at the chosen frequency to record displacement.
Plot the normal mid-membrane displacement (w0) as a function of the relative position across the substrate.
Construct a 3D colormap of the surface vibratory profile using Origin 8.5 data analysis software.
Sub-culture human bone marrow-derived MSCs in T150 tissue culture flasks at an initial seeding density of 4,000-5,000 cells/cm² in MSC maintenance media.
After 7-8 days of cell culture (to ~85% confluency), trypsinize the cells with a cell dissociation reagent such as accutase.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Centrifuge the cells at 440 x g for 5 min.
Re-suspend the cell pellet in fresh MSC maintenance media at a concentration of 4.5 x 10⁶ cells/ml.
Immerse the PCL scaffold in 70% ethanol overnight.
After solvent evaporation, expose both sides of the scaffold to germicidal UV light (254 nm) for 5-8 min.
Soak the PCL scaffold in a 20 µg/ml fibronectin solution at 37 °C for 1 hr.
Insert the fibronectin-coated scaffold into the silicone membrane.
Assemble the bioreactor as detailed in step 1.
Distribute 40 µl of the cell suspension evenly on the secured PCL scaffold.
Allow the cells to attach for 1-1.5 hr before adding an additional 1.5 ml fresh media to the vibration chamber.
Culture the MSC-laden PCL scaffold statically for 3 days.
Refresh the media upon completion of the static culture.
Impose selected vibration regimes to the cellular constructs.
Subject cells to a 1-hr-on-1-hr-off (OF) vibration at 200 Hz with a w0 of ~40 μm for 12 hr per day for up to 7 days.
Designate constructs subjected to vibratory stimulations as Vib samples.
Culture static controls in identical vibration chambers and designate them as Stat.
Collect 200 µl cell culture media from each chamber every other day (day 1, 3, 5, and 7).
Pool the aliquots from the same sample together (800 µl each).
Quantify cellular production of matrix metalloproteinase-1 (MMP1) using an MMP1 ELISA Development kit.
Quantify cellular production of hyaluronan (HA) using a hyaluronan competitive ELISA kit.
Assay the production of soluble elastin precursor following a previously reported ELISA procedure.
Remove the cellular constructs from the vibration chambers using sharp tweezers upon completion of the last vibration cycle at day 7.
Briefly rinse the constructs with cold phosphate buffered saline (PBS, 4 °C).
Incubate the constructs with propidium iodide (1:2,000 in PBS) and Syto-13 (1:1,000 in PBS) simultaneously for 5 min at room temperature.
Image the stained constructs with a multiphoton confocal microscope.
Separately, snap-freeze the PBS-rinsed cellular constructs on dry ice.
Extract the total cellular RNA using a previously reported protocol for gene analysis.
Verify the quantity and quality of the extracted RNA using a UV-Vis spectrophotometer.
Reverse transcribe 500 ng of RNA per sample into cDNA using a commercially available reverse transcription kit.
Perform the PCR reaction on a real-time sequence detection system using a commercially available PCR master mix.
Analyze the qPCR results using commercial qPCR data analysis software.
Employ multiple reference genes (YWHAZ, TBP, PPIA) as internal controls for reliable data analysis.
Take into account the variance of specific primer efficiencies in the analysis.
